correctness.rationale: Orthogonal monomials in normalized disk Bergman space have squared norm 1/(k+1); adding τ|f^(m)(0)|² modifies only coefficient m, so the exact kernel is (1-t)^(-2)-q t^m with q=τ(m+1)²(m!)²/[1+τ(m+1)(m!)²]∈[0,m+1). The disk zeros are the zeros of P_q(t)=1-q t^m(1-t)². For |t|=1 the factor t^m(1-t)² is -4 sin²(θ/2) exp(i(m+1)θ), and all positive-q boundary crossings occur exactly at θ=(2j+1)π/(m+1), q=1/[4sin²((2j+1)π/(2(m+1)))]. At each crossing Re[tF′/F]=m+1>0, giving strictly inward root motion as q increases, including multiple simultaneous crossings. A multiple root could only occur at t=m/(m+2), q*=(m+2)^(m+2)/(4m^m)>m+1, outside finite penalties. Hence the staircase counts all interior products with strict > thresholds; equality is boundary and excluded. The first threshold is 1/4 for even m and [4cos²(π/(2(m+1)))]^-1 for odd m; the q-to-τ inverse yields τ1=1/6 and τ2=1/132. Independent polynomial companion roots tested m=1..12 over admissible noncritical strengths, and checked physical thresholds. All claims are finite τ≥0 and m≥1; no multiple-jet norm.
